sapience_notes.subject: ~/.sapience/mcp.py token resolution
sapience_notes.value: TOKEN = os.environ.get('SAPIENCE_TOKEN') or _CFG.get('token') or '' at mcp.py:44 is a single module-level statement evaluated at import, before any CLI-flag or stdio dispatch. Confirmed mechanically (not just by reading) that all four named invocation shapes (--briefing-text, --receipt, --effect-line, bare stdio server) plus the --statusline auth probe authenticate successfully with SAPIENCE_TOKEN stripped from the environment, falling back to ~/.sapience/config.json's .token field. No shape requires the environment variable.

sapience_notes.subject: Measuring a secret-handling code path without printing the secret
sapience_notes.value: When mechanically verifying that a script resolves a credential from a fallback file rather than requiring the env var, record only length + a short SHA-256 fingerprint (e.g. first 12 hex chars) of the resolved value, never the raw secret -- sufficient to later detect a regression (value changed) without the record itself becoming a new place the secret is held in plaintext.

sapience_notes.subject: mcp.py stdio server auth guard location
sapience_notes.value: The bare stdio MCP server shape in ~/.sapience/mcp.py guards on `if not TOKEN: sys.stderr.write('Set SAPIENCE_TOKEN...'); sys.exit(1)` at mcp.py:2015-2016, immediately before the stdin JSON-RPC read loop and after every CLI-flag branch (--briefing-text, --receipt, --effect-line, --statusline, --stats, etc.) has already been checked and skipped. A successful `initialize` JSON-RPC reply is therefore proof the token resolved, without needing to read TOKEN's value.
